title: Differential basis quotient has vanishing localized cotangent obstructions
statement: Let R,D,Q be commutative rings, D a smooth R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and Q an R-algebra whose structure map R→Q is surjective. Let σ:D→Q be an R-algebra homomorphism, n≥0, and f:Fin n→D with σ(fᵢ)=0. Suppose 1⊗dfᵢ is a Q-basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of Q⊗_D Ω[D/R] [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], using σ for the D-action. Set a=(fᵢ) and C=D/a. Given a ring homomorphism τ:C→Q with τ∘(D→C)=σ, every prime q of C containing ker τ has H₁(L[C/R])_q=0 and Ω[C/R]_q=0 (the localizations of modules [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]).

source.place: Tag 07M7, second paragraph, the Jacobi-Zariski sequence and rank/Nakayama argument through H₁ and Ω vanishing

proof.text: Put a = (fᵢ), C = D/a and M = Ω[D/R]. Smoothness supplies H₁(L[D/R]) = 0 and projectivity of M. Apply the smooth Jacobi–Zariski quotient sequence to obtain i, δ, w, with i injective, i→δ and δ→w exact, w surjective, and δ([fᵢ]) = 1⊗dfᵢ.

Fix q containing ker τ, put S = C\q, L = S⁻¹C, and k = L/m_L. Surjectivity of R→Q and σ∘(R→D) = R→Q make σ surjective, and τ∘mk = σ makes τ surjective. The residue map C→k kills ker τ, since its kernel is q. It descends uniquely to ρ:Q→k. Install the resulting D→Q→k scalar tower. Base-change the specified Q-basis to k and cancel the scalar extensions. Identify S⁻¹(C⊗_D M) with L⊗_C(C⊗_D M), and then k⊗_L S⁻¹(C⊗_D M) with k⊗_D M. On pure tensors these identifications send the reductions of (1⊗dfᵢ)/1 to 1⊗dfᵢ. Thus these reductions form a k-basis. All maps and their pure-tensor formulas are written explicitly in Lean.

The module N = S⁻¹(C⊗_D M) is finitely presented and flat over the local ring L: finite projective M is finitely presented and flat, and both properties persist under scalar extension and localization. Apply Mathlib Module.exists_basis_of_basis_baseChange to the vectors (1⊗dfᵢ)/1 and their residue basis. Its Tor-injectivity hypothesis follows because tensoring the inclusion m_L→L with flat N is injective. This is the local Nakayama/flatness basis criterion: the specified vectors lift to a basis b of N. This avoids computing rankAtStalk or using local constancy of rank.

Prove by span induction that the classes gᵢ = [fᵢ] span a/a² as a D-module; surjectivity of D→C gives the same C-span. Localization gives generation by gᵢ/1 over L. Hence ψ:(Fin n→₀L)→(a/a²)_q, the linear-combination map, is surjective. The composite δ_qψ is precisely the linear-combination map of the basis b, so it is bijective. To prove δ_q injective, lift two source elements through ψ and apply b.repr to equality of their δ_q images. To prove δ_q surjective, lift y using ψ(b.repr y). No surjective-endomorphism theorem is needed.

Localize the Jacobi–Zariski sequence. Localization preserves injectivity, surjectivity and exactness. Injectivity of δ_q and exactness imply i_q = 0; because i_q is injective, its source is subsingleton. Surjectivity of δ_q and exactness imply w_q = 0; because w_q is surjective, its target is subsingleton. These are the two conclusions.

proof_origin.description: Complete Lean proof following Stacks 07M7. Uses residue-basis lifting for a finite flat local module instead of rank local constancy and a surjective endomorphism. Tensor-product transports, conormal generation and both exactness deductions are proved explicitly; no new holes or nodes.

Quotienting a smooth algebra by elements in a section kernel whose differentials form a basis modulo that kernel gives zero localized cotangent homology and differentials

lean.statement:
theorem localized_cotangent_vanishes_of_section_differential_basis
    (R D Q : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing D] [CommRing Q]
    [Algebra R D] [Algebra R Q] [Smooth R D]
    (σ : D →ₐ[R] Q) (hπ : Function.Surjective (algebraMap R Q))
    (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → D) (hf : ∀ i, σ (f i) = 0)
    (hb : letI : Algebra D Q := σ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
      ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin n) Q (Q ⊗[D] KaehlerDifferential R D),
        ∀ i, b i = 1 ⊗ₜ[D] KaehlerDifferential.D R D (f i))
    (τ : (D ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) →+* Q)
    (hτ : τ.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f))) = σ.toRingHom) :
    ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (D ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)),
      RingHom.ker τ ≤ q.asIdeal →
        Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl
          (H1Cotangent R (D ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)))) ∧
        Subsingleton (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl
          (KaehlerDifferential R (D ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))))
